title: Deploying new code while runs are in flight
purpose: A change to the workflow code can make every run that is waiting unable to continue. Replay recorded histories through three versions of the code to see which is safe, then deploy the safe one the way the design says: new runs on new workers, old runs finish on old workers. Finally, stop a worker politely and see that its step is not repeated.

steps.display: agentctl start --task '{"ticket": "T-1", "test_seconds": 2}'   # a run in flight on version 1
WORKFLOW_VARIANT=v1 agentctl replay --sessions s-2b3d20ee   # the code the run was recorded with
WORKFLOW_VARIANT=v2-unpatched agentctl replay --sessions s-2b3d20ee   # version 2, a lint step added after every file change, with no protection

checks.description: the original code replays the recorded history cleanly
checks.because: Replay runs the workflow code against the history with no worker and no side effect.

checks.description: the unprotected change cannot replay the run that is waiting
checks.because: The history says 'snapshot, then run the next tool'. The new code says 'snapshot, then lint'. Deploying it would have stranded every waiting run.

checks.description: the same change behind a patch marker replays cleanly
checks.because: The marker makes old histories take the old path and new runs take the new one.

checks.description: the run in flight kept its queue and finished on version 1; the new run used version 2
checks.because: A run is pinned to the queue it started on, so the old code only ever sees old histories and the new code only new ones.

checks.description: when the last old run finished, nothing was left on version 1, so its workers can be removed
checks.because: This is how an old version is retired: wait until its queue is empty.

checks.description: the step that was running finished on its own worker: it has one attempt
checks.because: On SIGTERM the worker stops taking tasks but lets activities in flight finish. Compare S03, where a kill gave two attempts.
